title: Exact statistical transmutation of quantum mixtures on a ring
authors: Wayne J. Chetcuti, Nathan Goldman, Patrizia Vignolo, Anna Minguzzi
abstract: One-dimensional strongly repulsive quantum mixtures exhibit non-trivial exchange statistics arising from the interplay between orbital and spin degrees of freedom. Using an exact solution, we demonstrate that in the single-impurity limit the wavefunction of Fermi-Fermi and Bose-Bose mixtures on a ring threaded by an artificial gauge field display exact anyonic statistics under exchange of the impurity with the majority particles. The resulting fractional exchange phase is fixed by the angular momentum sector selected through the applied flux. We find that the impurity momentum distribution coincide exactly with the anyonic one, independently of the bosonic or fermionic nature of the mixture, with the large-momentum tails encoding a direct signature of the anyonic statistical angle. Finally, we devise a quench protocol for reversible dynamical anyonization. Our results provide a path for realizing and manipulating anyonized states with ultracold atoms.
summary: This paper theoretically proves that one-dimensional, strongly interacting quantum mixtures on a ring can exhibit exact anyonic exchange statistics. By analyzing the momentum distribution and energy response to an applied magnetic flux, the authors establish a direct link between spin/orbital degrees of freedom and fractionalized statistics. This work suggests a pathway for realizing and manipulating anyon states using ultracold atomic gases.
main_problem: The study demonstrates the exact statistical transmutation of quantum mixtures on a ring, showing that their exchange statistics can be anyonic.
main_result: The wavefunction exhibits exact anyonic statistics upon particle exchange, and this signature is directly encoded in the momentum distribution tails and persistent current measurements.
method: The analysis uses Bethe Ansatz techniques (necklace Ansatz) to construct wavefunctions for strongly repulsive mixtures and maps these results onto theoretical descriptions of hard-core anyons.
model_or_system: The system models one-dimensional, strongly repulsive quantum mixtures confined to a ring threaded by an artificial gauge field. The Hamiltonian includes both orbital and spin degrees of freedom, allowing for the study of Fermi-Fermi and Bose-Bose analogues.
key_observables: Momentum distribution $n_\downarrow(k)$, energy spectrum $E_0(\phi)$ vs flux $\phi$, and persistent current $I(\phi)$.
important_parameters: Strongly repulsive limit, artificial gauge field flux ($\phi$), particle number parity ($N_p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the strongly repulsive limit where spin and orbital degrees of freedom can be decoupled for exact solutions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate wavefunction construction via necklaces; momentum distributions compare impurity results to anyonic predictions, showing characteristic tails; energy spectra show flux periodicity changes; and time-evolved simulations demonstrate coherent dynamics during a quench protocol.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general model Hamiltonian and using the necklace Ansatz for exact solutions in the single-impurity limit. It then compares these results to theoretical anyon models, analyzing momentum distributions and energy spectra across different flux values before concluding with a dynamical quench protocol.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete theoretical predictions—measurable via ultracold atoms—for observing fractional exchange statistics (anyonization) in controllable quantum gas setups by manipulating artificial gauge fields.
